issue_context.title: ActiveSupport::NumberHelper number_to_currency loss of precision in Rails 7.x
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce
```
require "bundler/inline"

gemfile(true) do
  source "https://rubygems.org"

  git_source(:github) { |repo| "https://github.com/#{repo}.git" }

  gem "rails", github: "rails/rails", branch: "main"
end

require "active_support"
require "active_support/core_ext/object/blank"
require "minitest/autorun"
require 'action_view'

  
class BugTest < Minitest::Test
include ActionView::Helpers::NumberHelper
  
  def test_large_number_to_currency
    large_string = "123456789012345678.91"
    
    assert "$123,456,789,012,345,678.91" == number_to_currency(large_string, locale: :en)
  end
end
```

or manually in console:
```
> include ActionView::Helpers::NumberHelper
> large_string = "123456789012345678.91"
> large_bd = BigDecimal(large_string)

> number_to_currency(large_string, locale: :en)
=> "$123,456,789,012,345,680.00"
> number_to_currency(large_bd, locale: :en)
=> "$123,456,789,012,345,680.00"
```

### Expected behavior
```
# (Rails 6.1.7.6)
> include ActionView::Helpers::NumberHelper
=> Object
> large_string = "123456789012345678.91"
=> "123456789012345678.91"
> large_bd= BigDecimal(large_string)
=> 0.12345678901234567891e18

> number_to_currency(large_string, locale: :en)
=> "$123,456,789,012,345,678.91"
> number_to_currency(large_bd, locale: :en)
=> "$123,456,789,012,345,678.91"
```

### Actual behavior
```
# (Rails 7.0.8)
> include ActionView::Helpers::NumberHelper
=> Object
> large_string = "123456789012345678.91"
=> "123456789012345678.91"
> large_bd = BigDecimal(large_string)
=> 0.12345678901234567891e18

> number_to_currency(large_string, locale: :en)
=> "$123,456,789,012,345,680.00"
> number_to_currency(large_bd, locale: :en)
=> "$123,456,789,012,345,680.00"

```

Starting in Rails 7, precision is limited to 17 leftmost digits. Previously string and BigDecimal input values with more precision were preserved.

https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/43098 looks like where the change in behavior was introduced possibly with `valid_float?` always performing a float conversion.

### System configuration
**Rails version**: Rails 7.0.8

**Ruby version**: ruby 3.1.3p185
comments:
I confirm that https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/43098 is the cause. 

Should we use `BigDecimal` for checking?
```diff
--- a/activesupport/lib/active_support/number_helper/number_converter.rb
+++ b/activesupport/lib/active_support/number_helper/number_converter.rb
@@ -1,5 +1,6 @@
 # frozen_string_literal: true

+require "bigdecimal"
 require "active_support/core_ext/big_decimal/conversions"
 require "active_support/core_ext/object/blank"
 require "active_support/core_ext/hash/keys"
@@ -174,7 +175,7 @@ def default_value(key)
         end

         def valid_float?
-          Float(number)
+          BigDecimal(number)
         rescue ArgumentError, TypeError
           false
         end
``` 

cc @flavorjones
^ Yes, but I think we should rename the `valid_float?` method accordingly too.

Hmm. I think the root cause is in `bigdecimal`:

```ruby
require 'bigdecimal'
require 'bigdecimal/util'

puts RUBY_VERSION # 3.2.2
puts BigDecimal::VERSION # 3.1.4
puts 123456789012345678.91.to_d.to_s("F") # "123456789012345600.0"
```

`123456789012345678.91` will already lose precision by default initializing as a Float to `1.2345678901234568e+17`  ~> `123456789012345680`

Avoiding forced casting to Float seems preferable to me, especially as this method is specifically for currency amounts.

review_comments: This is the big fix. The other changes are because this method was renamed since its return type was changed.

Would there be a problem with something like this?
```suggestion
          case number
          when Float, Rational
            number.to_d(0)
          else
            number.to_d rescue nil
          end
```

I recently ran into a problem where I'm using a ["lazy object"](https://github.com/HornsAndHooves/lazy_object) that gets passed to a number helper. Previously this worked fine, but now `BigDecimal()` is not converting the object, because it sees the number as a `LazyObject` instead of the nested object being delegated to.

If my object was sent `to_d`, it would behave as expected. Interestingly, `Float(lazy_object)` works, but `BigDecimal(lazy_object)` does not.
Can you define `to_str` on you object and try to see if it works? As per documentation https://ruby-doc.org/stdlib-3.1.1/libdoc/bigdecimal/rdoc/Kernel.html#method-i-BigDecimal

Since the lazy object wraps an Integer, I would need to define to_str on Integer which I would prefer not to do. I will just change my code to not give the number helper a lazy object, since I'm sure this is not going to impact many other people.
